findings.documented: Tokens are valid for 24 hours, so a single login is enough for one working session. There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Tokens expire in exactly 15 minutes (expires_in: 900), and the API actively returns a refresh_token meant for a secret refresh flow.
findings.how_found: Inspected the raw JSON response payload from a successful POST to /auth/login.
findings.impact: Frontend applications will unexpectedly log users out after 15 minutes unless an undocumented refresh polling loop is built.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page and limit. Collection responses are shaped with total, page, and page_size.
findings.actual: Pagination relies entirely on offset and limit query parameters. The response payload returns offset, count, and has_more booleans instead of pages.
findings.how_found: Tested the /v1/listings endpoint and observed the actual pagination metadata keys returned in the raw JSON response.
findings.impact: Standard 1-indexed page-based data fetching will fail completely. Applications must implement offset-based extraction loops.

findings.documented: Timestamps are ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Timestamps entirely lack a timezone identifier (Z suffix) and are served in local naive time (IST).
findings.how_found: Inspected the posted_at string format directly in the raw listings payload.
findings.impact: Time-based filtering calculations will be offset by 5.5 hours if dates are parsed strictly as UTC.

findings.documented: Area is in square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Several listings (primarily from the 'MAG-' source) have carpet_area values that denote square meters rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Identified properties with mathematically impossible square footage (e.g., < 250 sqft) for multi-bedroom houses.
findings.impact: Calculations for price-per-sqft are massively skewed and inflated unless the units are converted client-side.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: price_max returns a small floating-point number representing a larger denomination (like millions or crores) instead of raw integers.
findings.how_found: Calculated the costliest project and found a mathematically impossible raw rupee value of 97.8.
findings.impact: Frontend sorting or display of project prices will show completely wrong values to users unless mathematically scaled up.

findings.documented: is_verified means our operations team has checked the listing. Anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: Multiple 'verified' listings contain obvious real estate scam text demanding upfront token or booking amounts before site visits.
findings.how_found: Searched listing descriptions for scam patterns like 'token amount' and 'booking amount'.
findings.impact: Users could be actively scammed by fraudulent posts; frontend needs to filter these out client-side.

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: The total_listings count is demonstrably incorrect for exactly 126 different projects when compared to the raw listings data.
findings.how_found: Cross-referenced actual project_id counts downloaded from /v1/listings against the total_listings field provided in /v1/projects.
findings.impact: Displaying the API's project counts directly to users will show wildly inaccurate inventory availability.

findings.documented: Pre-computed aggregates for your city — handy for a dashboard screen.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns a 404 Not Found error and is completely unreachable.
findings.how_found: Attempted to fetch data directly for the Insights dashboard component and received an HTTP 404 error.
findings.impact: The frontend application must calculate all analytics manually from the raw listings dataset to display any insights.
